steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan/425°F). Cut 250g sweet potato into fries about 1cm thick, toss with a teaspoon of cornstarch, 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, then spread in a single layer on a tray.
Roast the fries for 25-30 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp at the edges.
Meanwhile, shape 180g ground turkey per patty and season with salt and pepper.
Cook the patties in a hot pan or on a grill for 4-5 minutes per side until browned and no longer pink in the middle.
Toast the burger buns cut-side down for a minute, then build each burger with lettuce, sliced tomato and a patty.
Serve the burgers straight away alongside the sweet-potato fries.
Cook or warm through 200g lentils, then mash roughly with a fork to a thick, cohesive paste.
Sauté 150g finely chopped mushrooms in a little oil for 8-10 minutes until softened and any liquid has evaporated.
Mix the mashed lentils, sautéed mushrooms and 50g breadcrumbs together, season with salt and pepper, and chill in the fridge for 15-30 minutes so the mixture firms up.
Shape into patties by hand and fry, broil or grill for 3-5 minutes on each side until browned and crisp.
Meanwhile, boil 300g potatoes for 20-25 minutes until a fork goes in easily, drain, then mash with olive oil, salt and pepper until smooth.
Toast the buns, then build each burger with a patty and serve alongside the mashed potatoes.
Season the beef patty with salt and pepper.
Preheat a grill or griddle pan to high and grill the corn, turning occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until charred in spots and tender.
Grill the beef patty for 3-4 minutes per side for medium, or to your liking.
Toast the burger bun cut-side down on the grill for 1 minute.
Toss the mixed salad with sliced tomato and onion.
Build the burger with the patty and serve with the grilled corn and salad on the side.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Toss 250g broccoli florets with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 crushed garlic clove and a pinch of salt, spread on a tray and roast for 15-18 minutes until charred at the edges.
Pat the steak dry and rub with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and the other crushed garlic clove.
Heat a pan or grill until very hot and sear the steak for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to your liking.
Rest the steak for 5 minutes before slicing against the grain.
Serve the sliced steak with the roasted broccoli.
Cut 200g chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces.
Heat a wok or large frying pan over high heat with a little oil, add the chicken and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes until browned and cooked through, then set aside.
Add the sliced peppers, garlic and ginger to the pan and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until just softened.
Add 300g cauliflower rice and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender.
Return the chicken to the pan with 2 tbsp coconut aminos and 1 tsp sesame oil, and toss everything together for 1-2 minutes until heated through.
Serve immediately.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan/400°F).
Cut the courgette, red onion and bell peppers into chunks, spread on a baking tray with the cherry tomatoes, drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil, scatter over oregano and season with salt.
Roast for 20 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften and char at the edges.
Slice the halloumi and tuck it among the vegetables, then return to the oven for a further 10 minutes until the halloumi is golden and the vegetables are tender.
Serve straight from the tray.
Rub the steak with olive oil, cumin, salt and pepper.
Heat a griddle pan or grill to high and cook the steak for 3-4 minutes per side for medium, then rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain.
Meanwhile, slice the bell pepper and char it in the same hot pan for 3-4 minutes until softened and lightly blackened.
Toss the mixed greens with a squeeze of lime juice and a little olive oil, then arrange on a plate.
Top with the sliced steak, charred pepper and sliced avocado, and finish with another squeeze of lime.
Preheat a grill or griddle pan to medium-high (around 200°C).
Score the fish two or three times on each side, rub with olive oil, season with salt, and tuck a few lemon slices on top.
Grill the fish for 4-5 minutes per side until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily.
Toss the courgette and peppers with a little oil and grill alongside for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred and tender.
Serve the fish and vegetables with a final squeeze of lemon juice.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut 250g sweet potato into wedges, toss with half the olive oil and a pinch of salt, and roast for 20 minutes.

Push the sweet potato to one side of the tray, add the salmon fillet skin-side down and the asparagus tossed in the remaining oil, then roast for a further 10-12 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and the asparagus is tender.
Squeeze lemon juice over the salmon and vegetables before serving.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut 250g sweet potato into cubes, toss with a little olive oil and salt, spread on a tray and roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and brown 200g ground beef, breaking it up as it cooks, for 6-8 minutes until no longer pink.
Season the beef with salt, then wilt the spinach or kale into the pan for the last 1-2 minutes until just softened.
Spoon the beef and greens over the roasted sweet potato to serve.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan/400°F).
Cut the courgette, aubergine, bell pepper and red onion into chunks, toss with 2 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt, and spread on a tray.
Roast for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Warm the cannellini beans through and stir into the roasted vegetables.
Crumble the feta over the top and serve.
Cook 90g brown rice according to the packet instructions, about 20-25 minutes, until tender, then drain if needed.
Steam the mixed vegetables for 5-8 minutes until just tender.
Warm the cooked lentils and chickpeas through in a small pan or the microwave.
Combine the rice, lentils, chickpeas and steamed vegetables in a bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil, season with salt, and finish with a squeeze of lemon.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the sweet potato a few times with a fork and bake directly on the oven rack for 45-60 minutes until soft all the way through (or reheat if pre-baked).
Warm the black beans and corn together in a small pan for 3-4 minutes.
Split the sweet potato open and fluff the flesh with a fork.
Spoon the beans and corn into the potato, then top with sliced avocado, a squeeze of lime and hot sauce to taste.
Rinse 80g quinoa and cook in twice its volume of water for 15 minutes until the grains are tender and the germ has separated, then fluff with a fork.

Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and roast the sweet potato, cut into cubes and tossed with a little oil, for 20-25 minutes until tender; bake the cubed tofu alongside for the last 15 minutes until firm and lightly golden.
Assemble bowls with the quinoa, roasted sweet potato, baked tofu, spinach, sliced pepper and cucumber.
Drizzle each bowl with the avocado-lime dressing to serve.
